description: ISPF, the statistics institute of French Polynesia, publishes geographic fact sheets built from the 2022 census and earlier censuses, with a selector for the territory, its five subdivisions, communes, associated communes and islands. Each fact sheet downloads as an Excel workbook and a PDF. The territory workbook has 42 sheets across population, families, housing, education, activity, employment and businesses. Housing sheets give the dwelling stock by category from 1983, individual houses versus collective buildings, principal residences by approximate building age from under five years to 25 years or more, rooms and tenure including social housing. Other sheets give households by number of cars, two-wheelers and boats, and the number of workers who work in a commune other than their own, a basic commuting measure. Coverage is territory-wide. Format and access: free XLSX and PDF, no registration. Licence: no licence statement was found. Caveats: the territory and subdivision workbooks downloaded, but commune fact sheet links returned 404 from the cloud; the census here has no utility tables in these sheets. Simulation uses: building age and house type by archipelago for cyclone and coastal flood exposure, and car and boat ownership for island transport planning. Related records: the SPC Pacific Data Hub census household counts with electricity access.

schema_summary: Sheets by theme: POP, FAM, LOG, FOR, ACT, EMP, DEM, DEN, RES, TOU. LOG.T1 dwellings by category (principal, occasional, secondary, vacant) 1983 to 2012; LOG.T2 category and construction type (individual house, collective building) 2007 to 2017; LOG.G1 principal residences by approximate age (under 5 years to 25 years or more) and house or collective building; LOG.T3 and T4 rooms; LOG.T5 building age; LOG.T7 tenure 1983 to 2012 including social housing; LOG.T9 households by cars, two-wheelers and boats; ACT.T4 workers working in another commune than their residence (2022).
